subject: Medford Square Parking Meter Oversight and Electricity Rates
overview: The Council heard extensive resident testimony regarding the city's problematic parking department rollout and rejected an ice cream social intended to celebrate the completion of the Medford Square parking meter project. Members also approved a water meter loan order and reviewed new municipal electricity aggregation rates designed to shield residents from rising utility costs.

items.title: Records and Subcommittee Reports
items.summary: Approved meeting records from September 27, 2022, and reports from the subcommittees on Housing, Parking, Climate, and the Comprehensive Plan.

items.title: 2022 State Election Warrant
items.summary: Approved the warrant for the November state election after a briefing from the elections manager regarding polling locations and early voting procedures.

items.title: Italian Heritage Month and Cultural District
items.summary: Approved a resolution celebrating Italian Heritage Month and requested an update from the administration on the feasibility of establishing an Italian American cultural district in South Medford.

items.title: In Memoriam Salvatore Albano
items.summary: Approved a resolution sending condolences to the family of the former State Senator and dedicated the meeting to his memory.

items.title: Police Promotion Recognition
items.summary: Recognized the promotion of Barbara D. DeCristofaro as the first female sergeant in the Medford Police Department.

items.title: Walk, Bike and Roll to School Day
items.summary: Recognized the annual event and requested an update from the administration regarding drainage issues and design defects at the intersection of Woburn and High Streets.

items.title: Domestic Abuse Awareness and Military Recognition
items.summary: Recognized October as Domestic Abuse Awareness Month and approved a resolution requesting October 26 be proclaimed Godfrey Chevalier Day in honor of the Medford aviator.

items.title: Sydney Street Industrial Mitigation
items.summary: Requested that the August A. Busch/Budweiser facility provide mitigation for noise, light, and illegal truck idling impacting residents on Sydney Street.

items.title: Parking Meter and Residential Permit Petitions
items.summary: Heard resident testimony opposing the installation of parking meters in front of private residences and St. Joseph’s Church, as well as complaints regarding the lack of enforcement and the cessation of physical window decals on Marion Street.

items.title: Winthrop Street Rodent Mitigation
items.summary: Discussed rodent infestations reportedly caused by Eversource construction on Winthrop Street and noted that the Board of Health has an updated pest management ordinance for street openings.

items.title: Water Meter Loan Order
items.summary: Approved a loan order for the replacement of water meters on its third and final reading.

items.title: National Grid Grant of Location
items.summary: Tabled a petition for a gas main relocation on Walnut and Metcalf Streets because no city engineer was present to confirm road restoration standards.

items.title: Parking Impact Assessments for Permits
items.summary: Requested that the administration include on-street parking impacts in the criteria for permit applications requiring Traffic Commission approval.

items.title: Sidewalk and Stump Repair Status Report
items.summary: Requested a status report from the DPW Commissioner regarding the progress of sidewalk repairs and stump removals funded by the council.

items.title: Electricity Aggregation Rate Update
items.summary: Heard a briefing on new community choice aggregation rates designed to shield residents from a 100% increase in National Grid's basic service rates this winter.

items.title: Zoning Legal Services and Lyft Hub Special Permit
items.summary: Referred the zoning legal services contract to a committee meeting and tabled a special permit for a Lyft rental car hub pending a review of excise tax registration and legal counsel presence.

items.title: Parking Meter Celebration Food Truck
items.summary: Denied a food truck permit for an ice cream social to celebrate new parking meters, with councilors calling the event tone-deaf and a misuse of city resources.

items.title: Traffic Supervisors Union Contract
items.summary: Approved the collective bargaining agreement for the traffic supervisors on its third reading.

items.title: Needham Bank Sign Appeal
items.summary: Approved a sign denial reversal for 270 Mystic Avenue with conditions including a 90-day review and a requirement that illumination be turned off at 11:00 p.m.

items.title: Park Medford Breach of Contract Review
items.summary: Requested that the administration report to the council regarding potential legal action against former contractor Park Medford for an estimated $150,000 breach of contract.

items.title: Internet Affordability and Crown Act Compliance
items.summary: Requested outreach regarding the federal Affordable Connectivity Program and a review of city policies to ensure compliance with the state law prohibiting hair-based discrimination.
